purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and process program for the authoritative municipal water-treatment plant asset, preserving a legible raw-water-to-distribution workflow, operator functions, maintenance access, residuals handling, terrain seating, and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: controlled site approach with perimeter security, staff entry, service-vehicle gate and a road connection appropriate to a municipal utility rather than a generic paved apron
raw-water intake interface and screening/headworks zone visibly precede downstream treatment so the process direction is inferable from player-scale circulation and equipment placement
coagulation or mixing and settling functions lead into clarifier or equivalent primary-treatment basins with supported walls, access walkways and drainage cues
filtration and disinfection zones follow primary treatment and connect credibly to finished-water storage and distribution pumping rather than appearing as unrelated tanks or machinery props
control room and operator workspace overlook or connect directly to principal process stages and contain monitoring, records and operating fixtures appropriate to a continuously staffed utility
water-quality laboratory and sample-handling area connect to operator circulation without interrupting chemical, maintenance or service routes
chemical storage and dosing spaces are segregated from ordinary public or staff circulation and include containment, service access and process-side connections
residuals and sludge handling include collection, dewatering or transfer functions and a service route that does not cross the principal clean-water workflow
mechanical shop, pump room, parts storage and maintenance staging support the process equipment through credible doors, lifting/service clearances and vehicle or cart access
foundations, basin edges, drainage channels, pipe trenches and grade transitions seat the plant into terrain without floating tanks, unsupported process equipment or a monolithic artificial platform
upper_program: elevated galleries, catwalks and basin walkways exist only where supported by columns, walls, trusses or process structures and retain guard edges and continuous player headroom
any second-floor operator, laboratory, electrical or administration rooms connect through an enclosed supported stair core with usable landings at every occupied level
roof and upper service zones distinguish process halls, pump buildings, chemical spaces and control volumes while preserving drainage and maintenance access
pipe racks, cable routes and utility bridges follow credible supported paths between process stages and do not terminate in open air or pass arbitrarily through occupied rooms

large tanks, clarifiers and filter structures may rise above grade, but their shells, access stairs and service platforms must remain structurally seated and functionally connected to the plant workflow
circulation: operator circulation forms a continuous route from staff entry and control functions through the principal treatment stages, sampling points and finished-water systems
maintenance circulation reaches pumps, valves, filters, basins, electrical rooms and mechanical spaces without requiring passage through laboratories or controlled chemical storage
chemical-delivery and residuals-removal routes remain distinct from ordinary staff movement wherever the site layout permits
service vehicles can reach maintenance, chemical and residuals areas through believable yard geometry and turning/clearance space
every occupied elevated level and service gallery retains a supported route to grade through architectural stairs, ladders only where genuinely appropriate to equipment access
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a municipal water-treatment plant through surviving basins, filters, pumping, control/lab functions and process-flow relationships
favor localized flooding, corrosion, pipe failure, basin-wall breach, collapsed walkway, roof failure, electrical damage, chemical-area damage and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
major structural breaches must use irregular fracture geometry with gravity-consistent rubble or failed equipment below and around the affected zone
damage to a wall, platform, pipe rack or opening must resolve all attached glazing, doors, signs, ladders and supported fixtures so no floating remnants remain
preserve at least one legible exploration route spanning intake or primary treatment, downstream filtration/disinfection, control functions and finished-water or pumping systems
damage may disable individual treatment stages but must not erase the entire input-process-output story or turn the site into an arbitrary collection of tanks
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

production_admission.note: Authored program is a prerequisite only. Do not add this asset to production-approvals.json until the authoritative v2 automated gate has actually been run and its passing evidence retained.
